title: Team detail
goal: Decide about one candidate team: see the working behind its match score, who is on it and where they sit, then take it or turn it down.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The team's name and code, and the two decisions — nothing else. The verdict used to sit here too, as a soft badge wedged between the title and two buttons, which made the answer of the screen its smallest element; it is now the first card of the content. Back goes to the catalog with the filters and the scroll position the coach left it in — the whole point of this screen is that it can be entered and left twenty times in a row without losing the list.

zones.name: content
zones.purpose: Four blocks in the order the question is asked, not six cards of equal weight. FIRST the answer and the team on one surface: the score as a Stat, the word for it as a Badge, the bar it sits on as a Meter capped at 22rem (across the full column it read as a loading bar), then a rule and the six facts that identify the team as MetaItems — code, contact, where they sit, headcount, the brief's grade, internal or client. A blocker prints there as a line with a warning icon rather than an alert bar: it is one fact about the team, not an event to interrupt for. SECOND the working behind the score, in two columns, deduplicated against everything above it — the page used to print the same finding three times (a blocker in an alert, its short form in the reasons, its long form in a facts table), so one list now takes the fuller sentence wherever two exist and drops what has already been said. THIRD what they are building: the SoT description with the grader's own reason, the tools and the stack as tags, and the project behind them. FOURTH the squad — roles, LEAP standing, AI certificates and badges, one card each. No photograph: the avatar was removed on 2026-08-18 because a face is the one thing on that card a coach already knows and it was setting the card's height, so the certificates a coach came to read were pushed into a second column. That roster comes from the portals through the coach's own session in the browser extension, and it starts BY ITSELF as soon as the extension announces itself; the button stays for a retry and for the coach who has no extension, and when the pull has not happened the same card carries the workbook's three columns instead. Never both: it was the same four people twice, the second time in a poorer form. Tool names render through airun's own <ToolTag>, which wraps the system's Tag and supplies the mark for the tools we have one for — an app component that renders a system component and supplies the wiring, which is the promotion rule working rather than a second Tag. That is why Tag is not in the list below: the screen no longer names it directly. This is what the separate vetting screen used to be: the same rubric judged in two places was two screens to keep in step, and the catalog made one of them the answer.

zones.name: aside
zones.purpose: ONLY for a team this coach already has: the facts that stay true whatever tab the work is in — where the engagement stands, who to talk to, what they use, and who is on the squad — so they sit beside the work rather than inside one tab of it. A candidate team has no work beside them, so the screen has no aside at all: a 20rem strip of facts next to a page that is read top to bottom was a second column with nothing to be beside. What the score was measured AGAINST (this coach's own row from the SoT Coaches tab: where they sit, which languages they coach in, who coordinates them) closes the reading column instead, quiet and last, because it is about the reader and the reader came for the team. When the sheet has no row for this coach, that block says so and the screen stops claiming a personal match.

zones.name: chats
zones.purpose: Every conversation with this team, in the tab that is about conversations. A team has SEVERAL Teams chats (the group chat, a DM with the lead, the one the client sits in), so the tab is a list of them beside the one you are reading, never a page with all of them stacked: three threads under each other read as one muddled conversation. The list row says what the chat is, whether it is asked on a schedule, how much of it is unread and when it last moved; the selected row is marked with aria-current, so what a screen reader says and what the eye sees are one fact. The pane beside it is the thread as it actually happened, read back from the message archive on disk rather than from a rolling snapshot of the last few, with the draft waiting to go out sitting at the foot of it as a composer the coach edits before anything is sent. How a chat is handled (asked weekly or only read, when, approve or auto, what gets a reply, instant notifications) sits INSIDE that chat in a disclosure, because the rules that suit the team's chat are wrong for the client's. Adding a chat follows one that already exists in Teams by its link; creating a chat is still the outreach flow, and the two are never confused. The coaches' chat of the programme appears at the foot of the same list, marked as shared, so a question already asked there is visible instead of being asked twice.

zones.name: dialogs
zones.purpose: The same two writes as the catalog, so a decision made here is the same event as a decision made there.

states.loading: Skeleton shape=block blocks in the two columns with one aria-busy on the page, because the catalog is re-read from disk on a deep link rather than handed over in memory.
states.empty: EmptyState icon=group when the code in the URL is in no catalog row — a stale link, or a team that left the programme — with an action back to the catalog. A detail screen with no record is not a blank page, it is a wrong address.
states.error: Alert tone=danger with the reason and a retry, same as the catalog: the same file failed to read.

data: one row of the catalog payload (tools/catalog.mjs), matched by team code: profile, fit.reasons, fit.flags, fit.facts (countries, overlap hours, language coverage, shared tools), roster, eligibility blockers
the coach's own SoT row, for the aside

behaviours.given: a team whose sources list the coach among the members (the source systems staff them on the project)
behaviours.then: the coach is left out however their name is ordered — a team never lists its coach as its own expert
behaviours.why: The rule ran on one path of two for weeks and a freshly assigned team listed the coach as a member.

behaviours.given: a team whose workbook code is 0115-UBS2-04OP and whose project is UBS2-04OP
behaviours.when: any portal pull asks about the team
behaviours.then: it asks with the PROJECT key — the full code answers 'not found' and overwrites good data
behaviours.why: Measured: every pull after 2026-08-17 read 'not found' until the key was carried on the team.
